title: Update minimum R version or add older R versions to testing
description:
I think that we should have some type of testing confirm the minimum R version. Current CI tests oldrel-4 which is 4.2.3 (about 3 years old).

The description file states that the package works back to R 2.10, but there is some code (at least `paste0`) that requires a newer R version. And, running testthat requires R 4.1, so ensuring that the package does more than load on an older version would require something to change the testing infrastructure.

https://github.com/r-lib/prettyunits/blob/a321ec23ea30b904540bb8b0d30f2a519512d90e/DESCRIPTION#L23

My preference/recommendation would be that we require the oldest version we are actively testing and that we try to keep testing back to 4.1.

title: Edge case audit of `pretty_round()` and `pretty_signif()`
description:
## 1. `digits <= 0` silently returns `"0"`

Base R clamps `digits` to a minimum of 1; `pretty_signif()` returns a value
that is simply wrong, with no error or warning.

```r
pretty_signif(123.456,  0)   #> "0"
pretty_signif(123.456, -1)   #> "0"
pretty_signif(0.00123,  0)   #> "0.00"

signif(123.456, 0)           #> 100    (base R)
```

## 2. `pretty_signif()` does not validate the length of `digits`

`pretty_round()` errors on a length mismatch; `pretty_signif()` silently
recycles, producing a mix of digit counts with no warning.

```r
pretty_signif(c(1.1, 2.2, 3.3), c(1, 2))
#> "1"  "2.2"  "3"

pretty_round(c(1.1, 2.2, 3.3), c(1, 2))
#> Error: digits must either be a scalar or the same length as x

pretty_signif(1.234, c(2, 3))
#> "1.2"    # silently uses only the first element
```

Root cause is the recycling in:

```r
bottomlog[is.na(bottomlog)] <- digits - toplog[is.na(bottomlog)]
```

## 3. Zero-length input returns the wrong type

Both functions are documented to return a string, but neither returns
`character(0)` for empty input. The `mapply` branch returns a `list`.

```r
typeof(pretty_round(numeric(0), 2))            #> "logical"
typeof(pretty_signif(numeric(0), 3))           #> "logical"
pretty_round(numeric(0), numeric(0))           #> list()
pretty_round(NULL, 2)                          #> logical(0)

typeof(formatC(numeric(0), format = "f"))      #> "character"   (base R)
```

This breaks `vapply(..., FUN.VALUE = character(1))` and `rbind()` of
zero-row results downstream. `ret <- rep(NA, length(x))` wants to be
`rep(NA_character_, length(x))`, and the `mapply()` call needs
`SIMPLIFY = TRUE` handling for the empty case.

## 4. Names are dropped in one branch but kept in the other; `dim` is always dropped

```r
names(pretty_round(c(a = 1.2, b = 5.6), 2))         #> NULL
names(pretty_round(c(a = 1.2, b = 5.6), c(1, 2)))   #> "a" "b"   (mapply branch)
names(pretty_signif(c(a = 1.2, b = 5.6), 2))        #> NULL

dim(pretty_round(matrix(1:6 / 7, 2), 2))            #> NULL
dim(formatC(matrix(1:6 / 7, 2), format = "f", digits = 2))
#> 2 3    (base R preserves dim)
```

## 5. Negative zero appears in the output

```r
pretty_round(c(-0.4, -0.0001, -1e-20), 2)
#> "-0.40"  "-0.00"  "-0.00"

pretty_round(-0.4, 0)
#> "-0"
```

This is intentional behavior, but it should be documented and tested.

## 6. `NA` in `digits` or `sci_range` gives a cryptic error; non-integer `digits` is silently truncated

```r
pretty_round(1.234, NA)
#> Error in if (digits < 0) ... : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

pretty_round(1.234, 2, sci_range = NA)
#> Error: missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

pretty_round(1.234, 2.7)    #> "1.23"    silently treated as digits = 2
pretty_signif(1.234, 2.7)   #> "1.2"
```

## 8. `sci_range` comparison is `>=` but the documentation says `>`

Both help pages state that scientific notation is used when
`abs(log10(x)) > sci_range`. The code uses `>=`:

```r
mask_sci <- xtmp != 0 & abs(log10(abs(xtmp))) >= sci_range
```

So exact powers of ten at the boundary switch to scientific notation when the
docs say they should not:

```r
pretty_signif(1e6,  6)                    #> "1.00000e6"   docs imply "1000000"
pretty_signif(1e6,  3, sci_range = 6)     #> "1.00e6"
pretty_signif(1e-6, 3, sci_range = 6)     #> "1.00e-6"
```

Either the code or the documentation should change; the `>=` behaviour seems
more useful, so the docs are probably the thing to fix.

## 9. Extreme magnitudes leak the binary representation

With `sci_range = Inf`, or with `digits` beyond double precision, the digits
past the ~17th are floating-point noise rather than zeros:

```r
substr(pretty_signif(1e300, 3, sci_range = Inf), 1, 25)
#> "1000000000000000498609832"

substr(pretty_signif(1.234, 30), 1, 31)
#> "1.23399999999999998578914528480"

nchar(pretty_signif(1.234, 400))
#> 326
```

Clamping the emitted digits at roughly 15–17 would fix this.

## 10. Malformed mantissa in the denormal range

The mantissa can come back `>= 10`, which is not valid scientific notation:

```r
pretty_signif(1e-320, 3, sci_range = 0)   #> "10.02e-321"
pretty_signif(1e-319, 3, sci_range = 0)   #> "10.00e-320"
```

Only reachable for denormals, so low priority, but it is a real formatting
break. A dense sweep found no such cases at normal magnitudes.

---

## Not a bug, but worth documenting

Rounding is inherited from base `round()`, so it is round-half-**even**, not
round-half-up:

```r
pretty_round(c(0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5), 0)   #> "0"  "2"  "2"  "4"
pretty_round(2.675, 2)                   #> "2.67"
```

This follows from `See Also round()`, but in reporting contexts half-up is
often the assumed convention, so an explicit sentence in `?pretty_round` would
save people a surprise.

## What was verified as correct

For the record, so this issue isn't read as broader than it is. Across 20,000
random values spanning 1e-8 to 1e8 at `digits` in {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}, scientific
mode emitted exactly the requested number of significant digits in every case,
with no round-trip error beyond the rounding tolerance. Also correct:

- magnitude-bump handling: `pretty_signif(0.9999, 2)` → `"1.0"`,
  `pretty_signif(9.999, 2)` → `"10"`, `pretty_signif(99.99, 2)` → `"100"`
- the exact-power-of-ten branch, from 1e-300 to 1e300
- `NA`, `NaN`, `Inf`, `-Inf` handling, including correct positioning within
  mixed vectors (the nested `ret[mask_manip][mask_sci] <-` assignment is safe)
- extra trailing zeros on large integers (`18949057` → `"18900000"` at
  `digits = 3`), which is the intended anti-scientific-notation behaviour
- negative values throughout

title: Feature Request: Numeric Value Rounding and Signif to Strings
description:
A limitation of results from the `signif()` or `round()` functions is that trailing zeros may be lost.  As used in #13, I have implemented functions `roundString()` and `signifString()` in my PKNCA package, but the package isn't a good fit for the functions since they are simply for making numbers into prettier strings (which has nothing to do with the purpose of the package around calculations for the kinetics of medicines in people or animals).

Would you be interested in a PR that would make something like `pretty_round()` and `pretty_signif()` functions that would give the character representation with the requested number of digits maintained?

title: Issues in pretty-printing lobstr bytes on R 4.0

# Problem

I am not sure if this is off-label usage of `{prettyunits}`, but I wanted to use it to pretty-print memory usage reported by `{lobstr}` in a `{cli}`-message:

```r
report_memory_usage <- function() {
      mem_used <- prettyunits::pretty_bytes(lobstr::mem_used())
      cli::cli_inform("Current memory usage in R: {.bold {mem_used}}")
  }
```

This works as expected on `R 4.4`, but not on `R 4.0`. Is this something that can be fixed in `{prettyunits}`? Or do you consider this to be out-of-scope?

title: Custom quantifier
description:
Related to #7, in addition to prettifying currency amounts I've also got a need to prettify population figures, so while in one case it's useful to have a currency symbol in another it's not. So I was thinking about whether there's a way to extend `pretty_num()` so that you could specify your own set of prefixes/suffixes rather than SI units. If you're converting monetary amounts you can use paste to add the currency symbol to the output if you need that.

Rather than hard-coding a specific style, providing a custom set of prefixes would help support different institutional styles - for example the [Financial Times has recently](https://aboutus.ft.com/press_release/ft-makes-change-to-style-guide) moved to using "mn" as its abbreviation for a million, while the OECD use "thsd", "mln", "bln" and "tln" for their quantifiers. Alternatively you could use it to writing out the quantifier in long form, as well as enabling multi-lingual support.

I was thinking maybe a named list where the names are the SI unit notation.

For example something like:

```r

x <- c(1234, 1.234e6, 1.234e7, 1.234e9, 1.234e13)

# short form FT-style abbreviation
prettynum(x, style = "nopad", custom_prefix = list(k = "k", "M" = "mn", "G" = "bn", T = "tn"))
#> "1.23 k", "1.23 mn", "12.34 mn", "1.23 bn", "12.34 tn"

# short form OECD-style abbreviation
prettynum(x, style = "nopad", custom_prefix = list(k = "thsd", "M" = "mln", "G" = "bln", T = "tln"))
#> "1.23 k", "1.23 thsd", "12.34 mld", "1.23 bln", "12.34 tln"

# English long form
prettynum(x, style = "nopad", custom_prefix = list(k = "thousand", "M" = "million", "G" = "billion", T = "trillion"))
#> "1.23 thousand", "1.23 million", "12.34 million", "1.23 billion", "12.34 trillion"

# French long form
prettynum(x, style = "nopad", custom_prefix = list(k = "mille", "M" = "million", "G" = "milliard", T = "billion")
#> "1.23 mille", "1.23 million", "12.34 million", "1.23 milliard", "12.34 billion"

# French short form (unicode)
prettynum(x, style = "nopad", custom_prefix = list(k = "k", "M" = "M", "G" = "Md", T = "Bn")
#> "1.23 k", "1.23 M", "12.34 M", "1.23 Md", "12.34 Bn"
```

One thing to consider is where a quantifier isn't named then it could default to the SI convention (perhaps throwing a to the user warning that this has happened), or perhaps convert the value to the nearest quantifier that is included in the list.

title: Pad p-values with space at beginning so decimal aligns
description:
When using the function `pretty_p_value()`, I'd like the resulting character to be aligned at the decimal point for nicer usage when printing tibbles or using gt() or kable() to print tables. Example of what I'd like this to look like (not implementation) is displayed in ps_f_alt below:

``` r
# remotes::install_github("r-lib/prettyunits")

library(prettyunits)
library(tibble)

ps <- c(1, 0, NA, 0.01, 0.0000001)
ps_format <- pretty_p_value(ps, minval = .05)
ps_format_2 <- stringr::str_pad(ps_format, 5)

pdf <- data.frame(ps=ps, ps_f=ps_format, ps_f_alt=ps_format_2)
ptib <- as_tibble(pdf)

pdf
#>      ps  ps_f ps_f_alt
#> 1 1e+00  1.00     1.00
#> 2 0e+00 <0.05    <0.05
#> 3    NA  <NA>     <NA>
#> 4 1e-02 <0.05    <0.05
#> 5 1e-07 <0.05    <0.05
ptib
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>           ps ps_f  ps_f_alt
#>        <dbl> <chr> <chr>   
#> 1  1         1.00  " 1.00" 
#> 2  0         <0.05 "<0.05" 
#> 3 NA         <NA>   <NA>   
#> 4  0.01      <0.05 "<0.05" 
#> 5  0.0000001 <0.05 "<0.05"
```

title: Feature request: Provide option to convert bytes on 2 or 10 base
description:
As we all know this:

```
Notation      Symbol    Value
1 kilobyte    1 kB      10^3  = 1000 bytes
1 megabyte    1 MB      10^6  = 1000000 bytes
1 gigabyte    1 GB      10^9  = 1000000000 bytes
1 terabyte    1 TB      10^12 = 1000000000000 bytes


1 kibibyte    1 KiB     2^10 = 1024 bytes
1 mebibyte    1 MiB     2^20 = 1048576 bytes
1 gibibyte    1 GiB     2^30 = 1073741824 bytes
1 tebibyte    1 TiB     2^40 = 1099511627776 bytes
```
it still creates often confusion when dealing with size related metrics within IT world. 

The prettyunits library should offer an option to use either 2 base or 10 base for its bytes conversion. The default (10 base) can stay as it is for providing backward compatibility, although a clear statement regarding this is missing in the documentation.

title: add functionality for big numbers
description:
Would you consider to add some functionality to `prettyunits`
like mentioned here https://bugs.r-project.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=16982

``` R
#Abbreviate some big numbers using a suffix "k", "M":
abbreviate_num <- function (i) {
    n <- floor(log(i, 1000))
    n <- ifelse(n>2, 2, n)
    paste0(round(i/(1000^n), 2), c("", "k", "M")[n+1])
}
abbreviate_num(222)
[1] "222"
abbreviate_num(1422)
[1] "1.42k"
abbreviate_num(14223)
[1] "14.22k"
abbreviate_num(14223323)
[1] "14.22M"
```

title: Feature Request: Color Naming
description:
I recently found myself wanting a way to convert a color to a human-readable name (to automate making captions for figures in reports).

I'd think that this would be implemented as follows:
* Take the color names from `colors()`.
* Clean them up to be more human readable (e.g. convert all the items like "aquamarine4" to "dark aquamarine" and add some spaces to items like "blanched almond"), and
    * This would be the "full color list".
* Simplify the full color list to a shorter selection of a smaller number of colors (how different is "azure3" from "gray" or "wheat3" compared to "tan", really?), and
    * This would be the "simple color list".

For any input color, find the nearest color name (using one of the algorithms here: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Color_difference) and return that to the user.  The user could optionally choose either the "simple" or "full" color list (defaulting to simple).

title: Feature Request: p-value prettification
description:
I often need to present p-values where small values are shown with a representation like "<0.001".  Would you be interested in me converting the code below into a pull request?

```r
#' p-values in a human-readable string
#'
#' @param x A numeric vector
#' @param minval The minimum p-value to show (lower values will show as
#'   `paste0("<", minval)`)
#' @return A character vector of p-value representations
#' @export
#' @importFrom PKNCA roundString
pretty_p_value <- function(x, minval=0.0001) {
  ndigits <- -floor(log10(minval))
  mask_min <- !is.na(x) & x < minval
  mask_over <- !is.na(x) & x >= minval
  ret <- rep(NA_character_, length(x))
  ret[mask_min] <- paste0("<", PKNCA::roundString(minval, digits=ndigits))
  ret[mask_over] <- PKNCA::roundString(x[mask_over], digits=ndigits)
  ret
}
```

title: pretty_dt breaks in case of "Time difference of NA secs"
description:
Consider the following example below. 

While `difftime()` considers it valid to have `NA` time differences, `pretty_dt()` does break with a rather ominous error message.

- It would be great to have `pretty_dt()` just return "NA" and not error out.
- If this is not possible it would be great to have at least a more informative error message that hints at where and why the problem is occurring (e.g. "pretty_dt: Sorry, do not know how to handle NA difftimes.")

```r
difftime(NA,NA)
## Time difference of NA secs

pretty_dt(difftime(NA,NA))
## Error in if (pieces[1]) pieces[1] %+% "d " else "" : 
##   argument is not interpretable as logical
```
